subject: Indian Polity
topic: Lok Sabha – Membership, Powers, Functions, Privileges
text:
Membership Conditions to be a member of Lok Sabha

  • Citizen of India.
  • At least 25 years of age.
  • Must not hold any office of profit.
  • He must not be of unsound mind/insolvent.
  • He must be a registered voter in any parliamentary constituency.

A member can be disqualified

  • If he voluntarily gives up the membership of party.
  • If he over rules the ‘whip’.
  • If he remains absent for 60 days without intimation.

Presiding Officers

  • Presiding officer in Lok Sabha is the Speaker (in his/her absence, Deputy Speaker). The members among themselves elect him/her.
  • The Speaker continues in office even after the dissolution of the Lok Sabha till a newly elected Lok Sabha meets.

The speaker has to vacate his office earlier in any of the following three cases

  1. If he ceases to be a member of the Lok Sabha;
  2. If he resigns by writing to the Deputy Speaker;
  3. If he is removed by a resolution passed by a majority of all the members of the Lok Sabha. Such a resolution can be removed only after giving 14 days’ advance notice.

Usually the Speaker, after his election cuts‑off all connections with his party and acts in an impartial manner. He does not vote in the first instance, but exercises his casting vote only to remove a deadlock.

  • Charges his salary from the Consolidated Fund of India.
  • The majority of the total membership can remove speaker after giving a 14 days notice. During this time, he does not preside over the meetings. After his removal, continues in office till his successor takes charge.

Powers and Functions of Speaker

  • The Speaker presides at the meetings of the House of the People as well as joint setting of two Houses of Parliament.
  • The Speaker gives permission to the members to speak in the house.
  • If the Quorum (presence of only one‑tenth of the total strength of the house) is not complete, the Speaker can adjourn the house.
  • He decides as to whether a bill is a Money Bill or not.
  • He appoints the Chairman as well as Deputy Chairman of all the committees of the house.
  • Speaker takes the final decision as to disqualify a member on grounds of defection.

Pro‑Tem Speaker

The first meeting after election, in which Speaker and Deputy Speaker is elected by Members of Parliament is headed under the senior‑most Member of Parliament, he is called Pro‑Tem Speaker.

Deputy Speaker

  • The Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha is the Vice‑Presiding Officer of the Lok Sabha, the Lower House of Parliament of India. He acts as the Presiding Officer in case of leave or absence caused by death or illness of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
  • The Deputy Speaker is elected in the very first meeting of the Lok Sabha after the General Elections for a term of 5 years from among the Members of the Lok Sabha.

Powers of Lok Sabha

  • Money and the Financial Bills originate only in Lok Sabha.
  • The confidence and no confidence motions can be introduced in Lok Sabha only.
  • Article 352 says that the Lok Sabha in a special sitting can disapprove the continuance of National Emergency, even when the Rajya Sabha rejects such a resolution.

Power, Privileges and Immunities of the Members of Parliament

Parliamentary privileges are special rights, immunities and exemptions enjoyed by the two Houses of Parliament, their committees and their members. Without these privileges the Houses can neither maintain their authority, dignity and honour nor can protect their members from any obstruction in the discharge of their Parliamentary responsibilities.

Parliamentary privileges don’t extend to the President who is also an integral part of the Parliament.

Parliamentary privileges can be classified into two broad categories:

  1. Those that are enjoyed by each House of Parliament collectively.
  2. Those that are enjoyed by the members individually.

Some of the privileges and immunities enjoyed by the members of the Parliament, are as follows

  • Freedom of speech in the House subject to the rules framed by the House. The members are not permitted to discuss the conduct of the judges of the Supreme Court and High Court, except when the removal of a Judge is being considered by Parliament.
  • Immunity from proceedings in any court in respect of publication of any report, paper or proceedings under the authority of either House of Parliament.
  • Exemption from liability to serve as Jurors.

subject: Indian Polity
text:
Sessions of Parliament

  • Begins with the consent of the President.
  • Gap between two sessions should not be more than 6 months. The Parliament generally meets in three sessions in a year, which are as follow
  • Budget Session (February-May) It is the longest session.
  • Monsoon Session (July-August).
  • Winter Session (November-December) It is the shortest session.

Termination of Sitting

  • Dissolution: The Lok Sabha is subject to dissolution. Dissolution takes place when the President exercises his power under Article 85(2). It can be dissolved by efflux of time i.e. on the expiry of its term of 5 years of the terms as extended during a proclamation of emergency.
  • Prorogation: It means the termination of a session of the house by an order made by the President under Article 85 (2) (a) of the Constitution.
  • Adjournment: It does not put an end to the existence of a session of Parliament, but it merely postpones the further transaction of business for a specified time, hours, days or weeks. Adjournment generally does not have any effect on pending business.

Joint Session

  • It is ordered by the President to consider a particular bill in case
  • – Bill passed by one house and rejected by the other.
  • – The amendments made by the other house are not acceptable to the house where the bill originated.
  • – When a bill remains pending or unpassed for more than 6 months.
  • Joint session of Parliament is presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. In his absence, by the Deputy Speaker, or in his absence by the Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha or in his absence any other member of the Parliament who is acceptable to both the houses.
  • Deadlock over the bill is resolved by a majority of the members of both the Houses of Parliament present and voting.
  • No fresh amendment can be done in joint session.
  • There is no provision of joint session for passing Money Bills and Constitutional Amendment Acts.
  • In Indian history, only three bills have been referred to the joint sitting
  • – Dowry Prohibition Bill — 1961
  • – Banking Service Commission Bill — 1978
  • – POTA Bill — 2002

Mechanisms of Parliamentary Proceedings

Question Hour

  • The first hour of a sitting of the Lok Sabha devoted to questions and that hours is called the Question Hour.
  • The questions are of three types
  • – A Starred Questions: It is one to which a member desires an oral answer from the Minister in the House and is required to be distinguished by him/her with an asterisk. Answer to such a question may be followed by supplementary questions by members.
  • – An Unstarred Question: It is one to which written answer is desired an oral answer from the Minister in the House and is required to be distinguished by him/her with an asterisk. Answer to such a question may be followed by supplementary questions by members.
  • – Short Notice Question: A member may give a notice of question on a matter of public importance and of urgent character for oral answer at a notice less than 15 days prescribed as the minimum period of notice of asking a question in ordinary course. Such a question is known as Short Notice Question.

Zero Hour

  • The period follows the question hours and it starts at the noon and its duration is one hour (from 12 noon to 1pm).
  • During the Zero Hour various issues of public importance are raised without prior notice.

Parliamentary Proposal

  • Calling Attention Motion: With the prior permission of the Speaker, any Member of the Parliament may call the attention of a minister to a matter of urgent public importance. The minister may make a brief statement about the matter or he may ask for time to make a statement later.
  • Privilege Motion: It is a motion moved by a member of Parliament. He charges the minister with committing a breach of the privilege of the house by withholding or distoring facts.
  • Adjournment Motion: It is introduced in the Parliament to draw attention of the house to a definite matter of urgent public importance and needs the support of 50 members to be admitted. It can only be moved in Lower House of the Parliament. It should not raise any matter which is under adjudication by a court.
  • No-Confidence Motion: It is a resolution introduced by the opposition claiming that the house has lost its confidence in the government. If it is passed, then government must resign from the office.

details.summary: Overview of parliamentary sessions, termination, joint sessions, question hour, zero hour, and parliamentary proposals.

subject: Indian Constitution
content:
- The Supreme Court held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended under Article 368, provided it does not alter the basic features of the Constitution.
- The Preamble has been amended only once: the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, which added the words **Socialist, Secular, Integrity**.
- The amendment was upheld as valid by the Court.

subject: Indian Constitution
content:
- **Article 1**: Defines India as a Union of States and describes its territory, including states, union territories, and any territories acquired by the Government.
- **Article 2**: Deals with admission or establishment of new states.
- **Article 3**: Covers formation of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
- **Article 4**: Provides for laws made under Articles 2 and 3 to amend the First and Fourth Schedules and related matters.

subject: Indian Constitution
content:
- 1953: State Reorganisation Commission set up under Fazl Ali; suggested reorganisation of 27 states into 16 states and 3 union territories.
- 1956: State Reorganisation Act passed; 14 states and 6 union territories created on 1 November 1956.
- Subsequent new states/UTs: Maharashtra & Gujarat (1960), Dadra & Nagar Haveli (1961), Goa, Daman & Diu (1961), Pondicherry (1962), Nagaland (1963), Haryana & Chandigarh (1966), Himachal (1971), Manipur, Tripura & Meghalaya (1972), Sikkim (1975), Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh & Goa (1987), Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Jharkhand (2000), Telangana (2014).

subject: Polity
content: The Constitution of India (Parts V & VI) establishes an integrated judicial system with the Supreme Court at the apex. The judiciary is independent of the executive and legislature, yet remains accountable within the democratic framework.

• Resolves disputes between the Union and the States. 
• Issues writs for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. 
• Original jurisdiction under Article 131 (e.g., Union‑State disputes, inter‑State disputes such as the Cauvery water dispute).

subject: Polity
content:
• Judges serve until age 65. 
• Removal: Only by Presidential order after both Houses of Parliament pass a resolution supported by a majority of total membership and at least two‑thirds of members present and voting, on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity. 
• After retirement, judges cannot practice in any Indian court.

subject: Polity
content:
• Salary paid from the Consolidated Fund of India (not subject to cuts except during a financial emergency). 
• Chief Justice’s salary: ₹1 lakh per month (as per the text).

subject: Polity
content:
• Judicial decisions and conduct cannot be criticised in Parliament, except during removal proceedings. 
• Chief Justice of India is appointed on the basis of seniority.

subject: Polity
content:
• PIL allows any public‑spirited person or institution to approach the courts for the enforcement of fundamental rights or matters of public interest (e.g., basic needs, environment, child labour, women’s rights). 
• Originated from *S.P. Gupta vs. Union of India* (1982) where the Supreme Court held that a member of the public may file a petition even without personal injury. 
• Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice C.R. Krishna Iyer laid down the conditions for PIL.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content:
**Union List** – 100 subjects (e.g., defence, foreign affairs, atomic energy). Parliament has exclusive power to legislate.

**State List** – 61 subjects (e.g., health, sanitation, agriculture). State legislatures have exclusive power.

**Concurrent List** – 52 subjects (e.g., criminal law, forests, education, marriage & divorce). Both Parliament and State legislatures can legislate.

**Residual Powers** – Subjects not listed in any of the above lists rest with the Union Government.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Any subject not included in the Union, State or Concurrent Lists is a residual power and is vested in the Union Government.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: States must comply with laws made by Parliament and cannot impede the exercise of Union executive powers (Articles 256 & 257). The Union can issue directives to states.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: All disputes between states regarding the use, distribution or control of water are decided by the Centre under Article 262.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: States rely heavily on the Central Government for finance. Although independent revenue sources exist, they are inadequate.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: The Union can borrow from within India or abroad within limits set by Parliament. State borrowing is limited and cannot be from outside India.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Six zonal councils were established under the State Reorganisation Act, 1956 to discuss matters of common interest. The Union Home Minister is the common Chairman.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Consists of Punjab, Rajasthan, Haryana, Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh and Delhi. Headquarter: New Delhi.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Consists of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh. Headquarter: Allahabad.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Consists of Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Odisha. Headquarter: Kolkata.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Consists of Maharashtra, Goa, Gujarat and UTs of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. Headquarter: Mumbai.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Consists of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala and UT of Puducherry. Headquarter: Chennai.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Created in 1971 by a separate Act of Parliament for Assam, Manipur, Tripura, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh. Sikkim was added in 1994.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Established June 1983 by the Central Government to examine the balance of power between states and centre. Headed by Justice Rajinder Singh Sarkaria.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: Established April 2007 to re‑examine centre‑state relations. Headed by former Chief Justice MM Punchhi.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: A mechanism to coordinate between Union and State agencies on common interests. Article 262 provides for its formation; formally established in 1990 after the Sarkaria Commission.

subject: CDS Pathfinder
content: The President can promulgate three kinds of emergencies: National Emergency, State Emergency, and Financial Emergency.

subject: Polity
content:
### National Emergency (Article 352)
- **Trigger**: President satisfied that a grave emergency exists threatening the security of India or any part of India (war, external aggression, or armed rebellion).
- **Proclamation**: May be issued for the whole of India or any part of the territory.
- **Imminent Danger**: Can be proclaimed even before the actual occurrence if an imminent danger is perceived.
- **Types**:
  - **External Emergency** – declared on the ground of *war* or *external aggression*.
  - **Internal Emergency** – declared on the ground of *armed rebellion*.
- **Duration**: No statutory time limit; can be extended indefinitely by Parliament.

subject: Polity
content:
### President’s Rule (State Emergency) – Article 356
- **Legal Basis**: Articles 355, 356 and 365.
- **Article 355**: Union’s duty to protect states against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure state governments function per the Constitution.
- **Article 356**: If the President, on a report from the Governor or otherwise, is satisfied that a state's governance cannot be carried out per the Constitution, a proclamation may be issued.
- **Article 365**: When a state fails to comply with a Centre’s direction, the President may deem that the state’s government cannot be carried out per the Constitution.
- **Time Limit**: State emergency cannot exceed **3 years** without parliamentary approval.

subject: Polity
content:
### Financial Emergency – Article 360
- **Trigger**: President satisfied that the financial stability or credit of India (or any part) is threatened.
- **Effect**: Executive and legislative powers shift to the Centre.
- **Historical Note**: Never invoked to date.
- **Duration**:
  - Initially **2 months**.
  - Can be extended beyond 2 months if both Houses of Parliament approve before expiry.
  - If Lok Sabha is dissolved at proclamation, it must be approved by Lok Sabha within **30 days** of its reconstitution, provided Rajya Sabha has already approved.
- **Time Limit**: No statutory limit; can be extended indefinitely.

subject: E-Governance
content:
### E‑Governance
- **Definition**: Application of Information and Communication Technology (ICT) to deliver government services.
- **Goal**: Move toward **SMART Governance** – *Simple, Moral, Accountable, Responsive, Transparent*.
- **Interaction Types**:
  1. **G2B** – Government to Business
  2. **G2C** – Government to Citizens
  3. **G2E** – Government to Employees
  4. **G2G** – Government to Government

subject: E-Governance
content:
### Mission Mode Projects (MMPs)
- **Context**: Part of the **National e‑Governance Plan (NeGP)**.
- **Definition**: Individual projects focusing on a specific e‑governance domain (e.g., banking, land records, commercial taxes).
- **Characteristics**:
  - Clearly defined objectives
  - Defined scope
  - Specific implementation roadmap
- **Purpose**: To achieve targeted transformation in public service delivery through technology.

subject: Polity
content: The **Finance Commission** is the constitutional body that recommends the principles governing the grant-in-aid of revenues to the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India. It submits its recommendations to the President, who then lays them before Parliament.

subject: Polity
topic: Parliamentary legislation on State List subjects
content:
Parliament may legislate on a matter in the State List **only** when any of the following conditions is satisfied:
1. The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution by a **two‑thirds majority** that it is expedient in the national interest.
2. For the **implementation of an international treaty**.
3. When **two or more States** request Parliament to legislate on the matter.
These are the only constitutional exceptions; Article 356 does **not** empower Parliament to legislate on State List subjects.

subject: Polity
content: The **President of India** **shall not** be a member of either House of Parliament. The **Parliament** consists of **the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha** (Article 79).

subject: Polity
content: Directive Principles are intended to establish **social and economic democracy** in India. They are not aimed at political democracy, which is secured by the Constitution’s democratic structure and Fundamental Rights.

subject: Polity
content: Fundamental Rights have **legal supremacy** over Directive Principles. In case of a conflict, the courts give effect to the Fundamental Right. Rights such as **Right to Education** are **not extended to foreigners**, and the **Right to Information** is available to **any person**, not only citizens.

subject: Polity
content:
The following constitutional provisions have a bearing on education:
- **Directive Principles of State Policy** (Article 45, 46, etc.)
- **Rural and Urban Local Bodies** (12th Schedule) – they are responsible for primary education.
- **7th Schedule** – Education is placed in the State List, giving States the primary responsibility.
(5th and 6th Schedules deal with tribal administration and do not directly address education.)

subject: Polity
content: The **Constitution (92nd Amendment) Act, 2003** added **four languages** – **Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali and Sanskrit** – to the Eighth Schedule, raising the total number of recognised languages to **22**.

subject: Polity
content: The **Speaker** can **adjourn** the Lok Sabha but **cannot** adjourn it **sine die**; prorogation and summoning are functions of the **President**. The Lok Sabha **automatically dissolves** at the end of its five‑year term even without a formal presidential order. The Speaker **continues in office** after dissolution until **immediately before the first meeting** of the newly elected House.

subject: Polity
content:
Parliament exercises control over public finance through:
1. Presentation of the **Annual Financial Statement** (Budget).
2. Passage of the **Appropriation Bill**, after which money can be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India.
3. **Supplementary Grants** and **Vote‑on‑Account** for interim expenditures.
4. Introduction of the **Finance Bill** to give effect to tax proposals.
(Periodic review by a Parliamentary Budget Office is not currently a constitutional mechanism in India.)

subject: Polity / Indian Constitution
content:
### Citizenship by Naturalisation
- **Application**: Must be made in the prescribed manner.
- **Eligibility Criteria**:
  1. **Full age and capacity** – applicant must be an adult with legal capacity.
  2. **No dual restriction** – cannot be a citizen of a country that bars Indian citizens from naturalising there, and must have renounced that foreign citizenship.
  3. **Residence / Government service** –
     - Either **resided in India for 12 months** immediately before the application **or**
     - Served in Government service for 12 months before the application, **and**
     - During the 7 years preceding those 12 months, the applicant must have **resided in India or been in Government service for at least 4 years**.
  4. **Oath of Allegiance** – must take the oath.
  5. **Good character** – must be of good moral character.
  6. **Language knowledge** – must have adequate knowledge of any language listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

*Reference: Citizenship Act, 1955*

subject: Polity / Indian Constitution
content:
### Citizenship by Incorporation of Territories
- When a **new territory becomes part of India** (following a popular verdict), the **Government of India** specifies that the people of that territory become **citizens of India**.
- No separate application is required; citizenship is conferred automatically by the act of incorporation.

subject: Polity / Indian Constitution
content:
### Loss of Citizenship (Citizenship Act, 1955)
Indian citizenship can be lost in **three** ways:
1. **Renunciation** – Voluntary surrender of Indian citizenship after acquiring citizenship of another country. Subject to conditions laid down in the Act.
2. **Termination** – Occurs **by operation of law** when an Indian citizen voluntarily acquires the citizenship of another country. The person **automatically ceases** to be an Indian citizen (Article 9 of the Constitution).
3. **Deprivation** – Compulsory termination by the Government of India of citizenship that was obtained **by registration or naturalisation** when the person is found to have used **fraudulent means** to acquire it.

subject: Polity / Indian Constitution
content:
### Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)
- The Government of India issues an **OCI card** to persons who satisfy **any** of the following:
  1. Currently a citizen of another country **but was a citizen of India** at any time after the commencement of the Constitution.
  2. Was a citizen of another country **but was eligible** to become a citizen of India at the time the Constitution commenced.
  3. Is a citizen of another country **but belongs to a territory** that later became part of India.
  4. **Descendants** – child, grand‑child, or great‑grand‑child of any of the above persons.
- **Exclusions**: Persons of **Pakistan and Bangladesh** cannot obtain OCI.
- **Recent change**: The **PIO (Person of Indian Origin) card** has been merged with the OCI card, giving OCI holders the benefits previously available only to PIOs.

subject: Polity / Indian Constitution
content:
### Non‑Resident Indian (NRI)
- Definition: An **Indian citizen** who holds an Indian passport and stays **temporarily** in another country for **employment, education, or other purposes for more than 6 months**.
- **Voting rights**: NRIs, irrespective of whether they have acquired foreign citizenship, are **eligible to vote** in Indian elections.
  - They must **register** by filing **Form 6‑A** with the electoral registration office.
  - To exercise the franchise, they must be **physically present** at their place of origin (i.e., their constituency) on the day of voting.

subject: Polity / Indian Constitution
content:
### Pravasi Bharatiya Diwas (PBD)
- **Date**: Celebrated **9 January** every year.
- **Purpose**: Recognises the **contribution of the overseas Indian community** to India's development.
- **Historical significance**: 9 January marks the day **Mahatma Gandhi returned to India from South Africa**.
- **Inception**: First celebrated in **2003**.
- **Recent edition**: The **14th PBD** was held on **9 January 2017** in Bengaluru, Karnataka. Attended by **Portugal Prime Minister Dr. António Costa**. Theme: **“Redefining Engagement with the Indian Diaspora.”**
- **Opportunities**: Provides a platform for overseas Indians to interact with the Indian government and people.

subject: Polity / Indian Constitution
content:
### Citizenship (Amendment) Bill, 2015
- **Date passed**: **9 January 2015** by the Parliament of India.
- **Objective**: To bring **parity** between the provisions for **Persons of Indian Origin (PIO)** and **Overseas Citizens of India (OCI)** card‑holders.
- **Key change**: Benefits that were earlier available only to **PIOs** (including recognition for **grand‑children**) were **extended to OCI card‑holders**, and the recognition was further expanded to **great‑grand‑children**.

subject: Constitutional Law
content:
# Habeas Corpus

- **Definition**: A writ that allows a person who is imprisoned or detained to seek a court order questioning the legality of their detention.
- **Purpose**: Protects personal liberty by ensuring that no one can be held without lawful authority.
- **Key Features**:
  - Issued by a court of law.
  - Requires the detained person to present evidence of the authority under which they were detained.
  - If the court finds no lawful basis, it orders the release of the person.
- **Constitutional Basis**: Article 32 of the Indian Constitution (guarantee of fundamental rights).

subject: Constitutional Law
content:
# Mandamus

- **Definition**: A writ of *mandamus* (Latin for “command”) issued by a court to compel a public authority or official to perform a duty they are legally obligated to perform.
- **Scope**:
  - Applies to public duties, not private actions.
  - Can command or forbid an action.
- **Typical Use Cases**:
  - Directing a government department to issue a license.
  - Requiring a public officer to file a report.
- **Constitutional Basis**: Article 145 (Supreme Court) and Article 136 (High Courts) empower courts to issue mandamus.

subject: Constitutional Law
content:
# Quo Warranto

- **Definition**: A writ that challenges a person’s right to hold a public office.
- **Purpose**: Prevents unlawful occupation of office.
- **Procedure**:
  - The court orders the person to show the authority under which they hold the office.
  - If the person cannot prove legitimate authority, the court can remove them from office.
- **Constitutional Basis**: Article 145 (Supreme Court) and Article 136 (High Courts).

subject: Constitutional Law
content:
# Certiorari

- **Definition**: A writ that orders the removal of a case from an inferior court to a superior court.
- **When Used**:
  - To correct jurisdictional errors.
  - To ensure that the inferior court has not acted beyond its authority.
- **Effect**: The lower court must transfer the case to the higher court for further proceedings.
- **Constitutional Basis**: Article 145 (Supreme Court) and Article 136 (High Courts).

subject: Constitutional Law
content:
# Prohibition

- **Definition**: A writ issued by a higher court to stop proceedings in a lower court.
- **Grounds**:
  - Overstepping of jurisdiction.
  - Violation of natural justice.
- **Effect**: The lower court must cease proceedings until the higher court directs otherwise.
- **Constitutional Basis**: Article 145 (Supreme Court) and Article 136 (High Courts).

subject: Constitutional Law
content:
# Advisory Jurisdiction (Article 143)

- **Who Can Seek Advice?**
  - The President of India.
- **Nature of Opinion**:
  - The Supreme Court gives its opinion on legal questions or matters of public interest.
  - The opinion is *not binding* on the President.
- **Purpose**:
  - To provide the President with a legal perspective before making decisions.
- **Constitutional Basis**: Article 143 of the Indian Constitution.

subject: Constitutional Law
topic: Types of Appeals to the Supreme Court
content:
# Appellate Jurisdiction (Articles 132, 133, 134)

1. **Appeal against any High Court decision**
   - Requires a certificate from the High Court that the case involves a *question of interpretation of the Constitution*.
2. **Appeal against civil cases decided by a High Court**
   - Requires a certificate that the case involves a *substantial question of law*.
3. **Appeal against criminal cases**
   - Applies when the High Court reverses an acquittal and sentences to death, or when it withdraws a case from a lower court and sentences to death.
- **Effect**: The Supreme Court can review the High Court’s decision and either uphold, reverse, or modify it.

subject: Constitutional Law
content:
# Review Jurisdiction (Article 137)

- **Scope**: The Supreme Court can review *any* judgment it has passed.
- **Transfer Power**: The Court can transfer a case from any court to itself if it involves an important question of law.
- **Parliamentary Powers**: Parliament may confer additional powers on the Supreme Court through legislation.
- **Constitutional Basis**: Article 137 of the Indian Constitution.

subject: Constitutional Law
content:
# Election Jurisdiction

- **Responsibility**: The Supreme Court decides disputes related to the elections of the President and Vice-President of India.
- **Typical Disputes**:
  - Allegations of electoral malpractices.
  - Challenges to the validity of election results.
- **Constitutional Basis**: Article 147 of the Indian Constitution.

subject: Polity
content:
### National Development Council (NDC)
- **Nature**: Open, extra‑constitutional, non‑statutory advisory body to the Planning Commission (advice not binding).
- **Presiding Officer**: Prime Minister of India (ex‑officio chairman).
- **Composition**:
  - Prime Minister
  - Union Cabinet Ministers
  - Chief Ministers of all States
  - Representatives of Union Territories
  - Members of the Planning Commission
- **Purpose**: Platform for decision‑making and deliberation on development matters across the country.

subject: Polity
content:
### NITI Aayog
- **Status**: Think‑tank of the Government of India; provides strategic and technical advice to both central and state governments.
- **Chairman**: Prime Minister (ex‑officio).
- **Key Functions**:
  1. **Foster Cooperative Federalism** – Structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the states on a continuous basis, recognising that strong states make a strong nation.
  2. **Village‑Level Planning** – Develop mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate them progressively to higher levels of government.
  3. **National Security & Economic Strategy** – Ensure that, where referred, national security interests are incorporated into economic policy.
  4. **Inclusive Growth** – Pay special attention to sections of society that may be at risk of not benefiting adequately from economic progress.
  5. **Stakeholder Partnerships** – Encourage partnerships between key stakeholders, national and international think‑tanks, and educational/research institutions.

subject: Polity
content:
### State Finance Commission
- **Mandate**: Review the financial position of Panchayats and recommend grant‑in‑aid.
- **Key Recommendation**: Submit its recommendations to the Governor of the respective state for implementation.

subject: Polity
content:
### Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
- **Purpose**: Establish a Lokpal for the Union and Lokayuktas for states to investigate allegations of corruption against certain public functionaries.
- **Composition of Lokpal**:
  - Chairperson + maximum of **8 members**.
  - **50 % judicial members**.
  - **50 % members** must belong to SC/ST/OBCs, minorities, or be women.
- **Selection Committee** (for Chairperson & members):
  1. Prime Minister
  2. Speaker of Lok Sabha
  3. Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
  4. Chief Justice of India (or a sitting Supreme Court Judge nominated by the CJI)
  5. Eminent jurist (recommended by the first four members).
- **Prime Minister**: Brought under the purview of the Lokpal.

subject: Polity
content:
### National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
- **Statutory Body** established in **1993** under an Act of Parliament.
- **Composition**:
  - Chairman (retired Chief Justice of India).
  - Four other members (multi‑member body).
- **Term of Office**: 5 years **or** until the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.
- **Post‑tenure Restriction**: After serving, the Chairman and members are **not eligible** for further employment under the Central or any State Government.

subject: Polity
content:
### National Commission for Minorities (NCM)
- **Established** under the **National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992**.
- **Recognised Minority Communities** (six):
  1. Muslims
  2. Christians
  3. Sikhs
  4. Buddhists
  5. Parsis
  6. Jains
- **Composition**:
  - Chairperson
  - Five Members, each representing one of the five minority communities (the Act originally envisaged representation for five; the sixth community is also covered under the broader mandate).
- **Additional Offices**: President and Vice‑President (as per internal administrative structure).

subject: Indian Polity
content:
### 73rd Amendment (1992) – Panchayati Raj
- Establishes **Gram Sabha** as the basic unit of local self‑government.
- Constitutes Panchayats at village, intermediate and district levels.
- Mandates **direct elections** to all seats in Panchayats.
- Provides **reservation** of seats for SCs, STs and women.
- Fixes the tenure of Panchayats at **5 years**.
- Strengthens decentralisation and grassroots democracy.

subject: Indian Polity
content:
### 74th Amendment (1992) – Nagar Palika
- Constitutes three types of municipalities: **Municipal Corporation**, **Municipal Council** and **Nagar Panchayat**.
- Provides **reservation** of seats in every municipality for SCs, STs, women and backward classes.
- Aims to promote inclusive urban local governance.

subject: Polity
content:
### Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog)
- **Established:** 1950 under the **Planning Commission Act**.
- **Nature:** *Advisory* body to the Government of India; **does not have any executive powers**.
- **Key Functions:**
  1. Formulation of the **Five‑Year Plans** and the **Annual Plans** for optimal utilisation of resources.
  2. Assessment of **resource gaps** and identification of factors that may **retard economic development**.
  3. Providing **policy recommendations** to the Cabinet.
- **What it does NOT do:**
  - It is **not responsible for the execution** of development programmes; implementation is carried out by the concerned ministries and the **Central & State governments**.
- **Abolition:** Replaced by **NITI Aayog** in 2015, but many exam questions still refer to the erstwhile Planning Commission.

subject: Polity
topic: Elements of the Annual Financial Statement (Budget)
content:
### Annual Financial Statement (Budget) – Core Components
| Element | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Estimates of Revenue Receipts** | Projected tax and non‑tax revenue for the fiscal year. |
| **Estimates of Capital Receipts** | Loans, disinvestment proceeds, market borrowings, etc. |
| **Estimates of Expenditure** | Planned spending on **revenue** (current) and **capital** (development) items. |

- **Ways and Means** (the **Ways and Means** statement) is a **separate document** that outlines the **methods** the government will use to raise revenue (e.g., borrowing, taxation) and is **not part of the Annual Financial Statement** itself.

subject: Polity
content:
### Commonwealth of Nations – India
- **Founded:** 1931 as the British Commonwealth; now a voluntary association of **54 sovereign, independent states**.
- **India’s Status:** A **Republic** (since 1950) but remains a member because:
  - **Article 2** of the Commonwealth Charter states that **membership is open to any sovereign state** that accepts the **principles of democracy, rule of law, and human rights**.
  - The **head of the Commonwealth** is a **symbolic position** (currently the British Monarch) and **does not affect the sovereignty** of member republics.
- **Implication:** Membership **does not compromise** India’s republican character; it is a platform for **co‑operation, cultural exchange, and diplomatic dialogue**.

subject: Polity
content:
### Election of the President of India – PR‑STV
- **Electoral College:** Elected **Members of Parliament (MPs)** and **Legislative Assemblies (MLAs)** of all states and Union territories.
- **Voting Mechanism:** Each elector casts **one preferential vote** that can be **transferred** according to the **single transferable vote** system.
- **Key Implication:** **Every MP/MLA has one vote**; the weight of the vote is **equal** irrespective of the size of the state’s legislature. The vote is **not weighted** by the population of the state.
- **Result Determination:** A candidate must secure **more than 50% of the total valid votes** after transfers.

subject: Polity
topic: Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India
content:
### Original Jurisdiction – Supreme Court of India
- **Constitutional Provision:** Article **131**.
- **Scope:** The Supreme Court has **original jurisdiction** in **disputes**:
  1. **Between the Government of India and one or more States**.
  2. **Between two or more States** (including Union Territories).
- **Exclusions:** It does **not** have original jurisdiction over:
  - **Treaties & agreements** (these are dealt with under the **executive** domain).
  - **Implementation of Directive Principles** (non‑justiciable).
  - **Bills passed by Parliament** (subject to judicial review, not original jurisdiction).

subject: Polity
topic: Role of the Pro‑Tem Speaker of Lok Sabha
content:
### Pro‑Tem Speaker – Lok Sabha
- **Appointment:** The **President** appoints a senior member of the newly elected Lok Sabha as **Pro‑Tem Speaker**.
- **Primary Duties:**
  1. **Administer oath** to all newly elected members.
  2. **Preside over the first meeting** of the House until a **regular Speaker** is elected.
- **Limitations:** The Pro‑Tem Speaker **does not conduct regular proceedings**, **does not give assent** to bills, and **does not have any permanent powers** beyond the initial convening.

subject: Polity
content:
### Inter‑State Council (ISC)
- **Constitutional Basis:** **Article 263** empowers Parliament to **establish an Inter‑State Council**; however, the Council itself is **created by legislation** (the **Inter‑State Council Act, 2006**), not directly by the Constitution.
- **Nature:** **Recommendatory** body – its recommendations are **not binding** on the Union or States.
- **Standing Committee:** A **Standing Committee of the Council** exists, **chaired by the Prime Minister**, to **process matters** and **prepare agenda items** for the Council’s consideration.
- **Purpose:** To **promote cooperation**, **resolve disputes**, and **coordinate policies** between the Centre and the States.

subject: Polity
topic: Jurisdiction of CAT under Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985
content:
### Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)
- **Established under:** *Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985*.
- **Purpose:** To adjudicate service‑related disputes and complaints of persons appointed to public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the Union **except** members of the Defence Services.
- **Key Point:** CAT does **not** entertain cases of defence personnel; they are dealt with by separate military tribunals.
- **Reference:** Section 2(1)(c) of the Act.

---

subject: Polity
content:
### Single Integrated System of Courts
1. **No double system** – unlike the United States, India does **not** have a separate federal and state court system.
2. **Constitutional provision:** Article 214 establishes a *single* hierarchy of courts for the Union and the States.
3. **Sub‑ordinate judiciary:** While the overall structure is uniform, the *organisation* of the sub‑ordinate courts (e.g., District Courts, Sessions Courts) may vary slightly from state to state due to state legislation.

---

subject: Polity
content:
### Committees of Parliament
| Committee | Type | Function |
|-----------|------|----------|
| Public Accounts Committee (PAC) | Standing Committee of Lok Sabha | Examines the accounts of the government and audits reports of the Comptroller & Auditor General. |
| Estimates Committee | Standing Committee of Lok Sabha | Scrutinises the budget estimates and suggests economies. |
| Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU) | Standing Committee of Lok Sabha | Examines the reports and accounts of public sector enterprises. |

All three are **Committees of Parliament**.
---

subject: Polity
content:
### Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) – Term of Office
- **Constitutional provision:** Article 324(2).
- **Tenure:** *Six years* **or** until the age of *65 years*, whichever is earlier.
- The CEC holds office **not** at the pleasure of the President; the term is fixed to ensure independence.
---

subject: Polity
content:
### Writ of Prohibition
- **Issued by:** A *superior* court (e.g., High Court or Supreme Court).
- **Purpose:** To **prevent** an inferior court, tribunal, or quasi‑judicial body from **exceeding its jurisdiction** or acting contrary to principles of natural justice.
- **Effect:** The inferior authority must **stop** the proceeding; the writ does **not** direct any action, only restrains.
---

subject: Polity
content:
## The Union Executive
- **Components**: President, Vice‑President, Council of Ministers (headed by the Prime Minister) – they aid and advise the President.
- **President** (Articles 52‑78): Highest executive authority of the Union. All executive powers of the Union are vested in the President and all executive actions are taken in his/her name. The President is the **head of state**, represents the Republic of India and is the **first citizen** of India.

subject: Polity
content:
### Eligibility Criteria
1. Must be a **citizen of India**.
2. Must have attained the age of **35 years**.
3. Must **not hold any office of profit** under the Government of India or any State Government.
4. Must be **qualified to become a member of the Lok Sabha** (i.e., not disqualified under any law).

subject: Polity
content:
### Electoral College
- Consists of **elected members** of:
  - Both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha)
  - Legislative Assemblies of all States
  - Legislative Assemblies of Union Territories of **Delhi** and **Puducherry**
- **Nominated members** do **not** participate.

### Method of Election
- **Proportional representation** by **single transferable vote** (STV) with a **secret ballot**.
- A candidate must secure **at least 50 % of the total valid votes** to be declared elected.

### Value of Votes
- **Value of an MLA’s vote** = \( \frac{\text{State population}}{\text{Total elected MLAs of the state}} \times 1000 \)
- **Value of an MP’s vote** = \( \frac{\text{Total value of all MLA votes (all states)}}{\text{Total number of elected MPs (Lok Sabha + Rajya Sabha)}} \)
- This formula balances the weight of **states** and the **Parliament**.

### Other Provisions
- **Supreme Court** has exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate disputes concerning the presidential election.
- The President takes the oath **in the presence of the Chief Justice of India**; if unavailable, the **senior-most Supreme Court judge** administers the oath.

subject: Polity
content:
### Term of Office (Article 56)
- The President holds office for **5 years**.
- **No limit** on the number of terms a person may serve.
- The President may **resign** by addressing a letter to the Vice‑President.

### Salary
- As of **11 September 2008**, the President’s salary was increased to **₹1,50,000 per month**.

### Impeachment (Article 61)
- Grounds: **Violation of the Constitution**.
- **Initiation**: Either House of Parliament can start the process.
- **Notice**: Must be signed by **at least one‑fourth** of the total members of that House and served to the President **14 days** before the motion.
- **Procedure**:
  1. The motion must be passed by a **two‑thirds majority** of the total membership of the initiating House.
  2. The other House forms a **Committee** to investigate the charges.
  3. The President may **defend** himself/herself, either personally or through the **Attorney General of India** or any other lawyer.
- The process is **quasi‑judicial** in nature.

### Vacancy (Article 62)
- If the office becomes vacant due to death, resignation, removal, or otherwise, the **Vice‑President** acts as President until a new President is elected.

subject: Polity
content:
### President – The Apex of the Indian Democratic Structure
- The President holds a **ceremonial yet pivotal** position in India’s democracy.
- While the Constitution vests extensive powers on the President, **in practice most are exercised on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers**.
- The President’s role spans **executive, legislative, judicial, financial, diplomatic, military and emergency domains**.

subject: Polity
content:
### Executive Powers of the President
- **Appointment of the Prime Minister** – the leader who enjoys majority support in the Lok Sabha.
- **Council of Ministers** – appoints members and allocates portfolios on the Prime Minister’s advice.
- **Judicial Appointments** – appoints the Chief Justice of India, Supreme Court judges, and High Court judges.
- **Other Constitutional Posts** – Chairman & members of UPSC, CAG, Attorney General, Chief Election Commissioner, other Election Commission members, Governors, Finance Commission members, Ambassadors, etc.
- **Information Right** – may request any information on Union administration and legislative proposals from the Prime Minister.

subject: Polity
content:
### Legislative Powers of the President
- **Integral Part of Parliament** – though Parliament drafts laws, the President influences the process.
- **Summoning & Dissolution** – can summon, prorogue, and dissolve the Lok Sabha.
- **Joint Sitting** – may summon a joint sitting of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha (presided over by the Lok Sabha Speaker).
- **Nomination to Rajya Sabha & Lok Sabha**
  - 12 members to Rajya Sabha (persons with special knowledge/experience in literature, science, art, social service).
  - 2 Anglo‑Indian members to Lok Sabha (now discontinued by the 104th Constitutional Amendment).
- **Address & Reports** – can address Parliament and lay reports on the floor.
- **Prior Consent** – required for certain bills (e.g., Money Bills).
- **Ordinances (Article 123)** – may promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session; they have the same force as an Act but are temporary.

subject: Polity
content:
### Judicial Powers – Pardoning Power
| Power | Effect | Example |
|-------|--------|---------|
| **Pardon** | Removes conviction & sentence; offender is completely absolved. | Full remission of a death sentence. |
| **Reprieve** | Stay of execution pending further consideration. | Temporary stay of hanging. |
| **Remission** | Reduces the period of sentence without altering its nature. | 2‑year rigorous imprisonment reduced to 1 year. |
| **Respite** | Grants a lesser sentence on special grounds (e.g., pregnancy). | Reducing penalty for a pregnant offender. |
| **Commutation** | Substitutes a harsher punishment with a milder one. | Death sentence commuted to life imprisonment. |
- The President can exercise these powers **under central laws**.

subject: Polity
content:
### Financial Powers of the President
- **Money Bills** – can originate only on the President’s recommendation.
- **Finance Commission** – appoints a Finance Commissioner every five years.
- **Contingency Fund** – may authorize advances from the Contingency Fund of India to meet unforeseen expenditures.

subject: Polity
content:
### Diplomatic Powers of the President
- **Treaties & Agreements** – concludes all international treaties and agreements on behalf of India.
- **Representation** – represents India at international forums and conferences.
- **Ambassadors** – appoints ambassadors to foreign countries and receives foreign diplomatic representatives.

subject: Polity
content:
### Military Powers of the President
- **Supreme Commander** – head of the Indian Armed Forces.
- **Appointments** – appoints Chiefs of Army, Navy, and Air Force.
- **War & Peace** – can declare war or conclude peace **subject to parliamentary approval**.

subject: Polity
content:
### Emergency Powers of the President
| Emergency | Constitutional Provision | Trigger |
|-----------|--------------------------|---------|
| **National Emergency** | Article 352 | War, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
| **President’s Rule (Constitutional Emergency)** | Article 356 | Failure of constitutional machinery in a state.
| **Financial Emergency** | Article 360 | Threat to financial stability or credit of India.
- **Procedure** – The President may proclaim an emergency **only after a written recommendation from the Cabinet**.

subject: Indian Polity
content:
### Absolute Veto

- The President can **decline to give assent** to any Bill passed by Parliament **except a Money Bill**.
- This power is exercised **once** and is **final**.
- The Bill is returned to Parliament without any changes.
- The President is not required to provide reasons for the veto.

subject: Indian Polity
content:
### Suspensive Veto

- The President can **resend** a Bill (other than a Money Bill) to Parliament for further consideration.
- The President may attach a **message** requesting amendments to specific provisions.
- If Parliament passes the Bill again (with or without amendments), the President **must** give assent.
- This power allows the President to influence the content of legislation while still respecting parliamentary sovereignty.

subject: Indian Polity
content:
### Pocket Veto

- Used when the President feels the ruling party may face instability and may be reluctant to assent to a Bill.
- The Bill is **kept in the President’s office indefinitely** without any communication to the Council of Ministers or Parliament.
- **Cannot be used** for Money Bills (President may assent or decline but cannot return) or Constitutional Amendment Bills (President must assent).
- The Bill remains in the President’s possession until a decision is taken.

subject: Indian Polity
content:
### Additional Powers of the President

- **Refer a decision** of an individual minister to the Council of Ministers for collective consideration.
- **Summon both Houses** of Parliament when they do not meet regularly.
- **Return the advice** of the Council of Ministers once for reconsideration.
- **Return a Bill** passed by Parliament once for reconsideration.
- These powers enable the President to maintain checks and balances within the executive and legislative branches.

subject: Indian Polity
content:
### Notable Presidents of India

- **Zakir Hussain** and **Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed** died while in office.
- **Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy** is the only President elected unopposed.
- **Neelam Sanjeeva Reddy** also served as Speaker of the Lok Sabha before becoming President.
- **Justice Hidayatullah** is the only Chief Justice who acted as President.
- **Dr. Rajendra Prasad** is the only President elected twice.

subject: Indian Polity
content:
### Functions of the Vice-President

- **Ex‑officio Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha.
- All bills, resolutions, and motions in the Rajya Sabha require his consent.
- In the **absence or illness** of the President, the Vice-President performs the President’s functions.
- If the President resigns or dies, the Vice-President **acts as President** until a new President is elected.

subject: Indian Polity
content:
• Judges of one High Court can be transferred to another High Court.
• Removal of a High Court judge follows the same procedure as for a Supreme Court judge: Parliament must pass a resolution by a two‑thirds majority of members present and voting.

subject: Indian Polity
content:
High Courts enjoy the following jurisdictions and powers:
- **Original jurisdiction**
- **Writ jurisdiction**
- **Appellate jurisdiction**
- **Supervisory jurisdiction**
- **Control over subordinate courts**
